package_info.why_malicious: No specific malicious package is described in this report. The article discusses general risks and incidents in the software supply chain, such as zero-day exploits, misconfigured cloud services, open-source and container image exploits, secrets theft, and API data breaches. The focus is on the challenges organizations face in securing their software supply chain, not on a particular malicious package.

behavioral_signatures: Zero-day exploitation of vulnerabilities in third-party code
Abuse of open-source software and container images
Theft of secrets, passwords, and tokens from source code repositories
API data breaches via third-party software
file_indicators: Sensitive files in source code repositories (e.g., .env, config.json, secrets.yaml)
SBOM (Software Bill of Materials) files missing or outdated
network_indicators: Unexpected outbound connections from build or CI/CD environments
API calls to unknown or suspicious third-party services
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized access to sensitive files and secrets in source code repositories. Continuously scan open-source and third-party components for vulnerabilities. Track and alert on unexpected outbound network connections from build, CI/CD, and production environments. Ensure SBOMs are generated and kept up to date for all software components. Use binary analysis tools to inspect third-party and vendor-supplied binaries for hidden risks.
